inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat request, authenticated via company SSO

instructions.note: The prompt explicitly instructs the agent not to ask for confirmation before irreversible production actions ('Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy'), removing any human-in-the-loop checkpoint and relying solely on instruction compliance.
The prompt grants the agent authority to execute irreversible production changes purely on the basis of a chat request, with no additional verification of intent beyond the engineer's SSO identity.

controls.name: Cloud audit log recording production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Logging occurs outside the model and does not depend on model capability, but every production action is recorded under the requesting engineer's name regardless of whether the engineer or the agent initiated it, so it does not resolve repudiation.

controls.name: Chat transcript as record of request intent
controls.decay_rationale: The transcript is recorded outside the model, but engineers can delete their own chat history, removing the only record of what was asked and why, independent of model capability.

controls.name: Human approval gate for irreversible migrations

findings.title: Shared personal credential plus a deletable transcript erases attribution for irreversible production actions

forecast.watch_signal: Watch for a move from per-engineer personal access tokens to a shared or service-account credential (further erasing which human the agent acted for), or for chat transcript retention/deletion policy changes that widen who can erase the only record of intent.

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on-call engineer's personal access token for every production action, and the cloud audit log records the action under the engineer's name regardless of whether the engineer or the agent initiated it.
The chat transcript is described as the only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted, and engineers can delete their own chat history, removing that record entirely.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so a migration decision that cannot later be attributed to agent or human also cannot be undone.
The system prompt instructs the agent not to ask for confirmation before acting, removing any human-in-the-loop checkpoint that could otherwise create an independent record of intent.

recommendations.action: Record a tamper-evident, write-once provenance entry for every agent-initiated action that distinguishes it from direct human action, stored independently of the requesting engineer's ability to delete it.
Require a raw-action human approval step, reviewed by someone other than the requesting engineer, before running irreversible production database migrations.
Retain chat transcripts in a store the requesting engineer cannot delete, so the record of intent survives independent of the engineer's own history controls.

findings.title: No rate, spend, or step limit on irreversible production actions

forecast.watch_signal: Watch for the agent being allowed to chain multiple deploy/migrate actions within one session without a fresh engineer request (longer_task_horizon), or for max_unattended_steps/max_runtime_minutes remaining unset as usage volume grows.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to deploy or migrate whenever asked, without confirmation, and no artifact states a limit on how many such production actions may be performed in a session or per day.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so repeated or rapid migrations with no rate or step limit could cause cascading, irreversible production damage.

recommendations.action: Enforce a hard limit on the number of irreversible production actions (deploys and migrations) permitted per session or per day, enforced outside the model.

stride_coverage.rationale: The agent cannot modify its own configuration or instructions (autonomy.can_modify_own_config is false), and no tool or server definition update mechanism is described in these artifacts.
Neither capability sends data outside the production environment the engineer already has access to; both are execute actions on infrastructure, not data egress.
credential_scope is user_delegated: the agent acts only with the requesting engineer's own existing production credentials and cannot exceed them.
Only the requesting engineer and the agent itself are described as having access to the chat transcript; no other party or external store is named in these artifacts.
The artifacts do not describe retention limits, storage capacity, or availability guarantees for the chat transcript store.
The artifacts do not state whether the cloud audit log is append-only or otherwise protected from modification after the fact.
Access controls governing who can read the cloud audit log are not described in these artifacts.
Retention and capacity limits for the cloud audit log are not described in these artifacts.

rating.rationale: All inputs to this agent come from authenticated, trusted on-call engineers; there is no untrusted or injected content in its context, so no complete attack path from an untrusted source to a sensitive sink exists today. The risk instead comes from two missing properties on consequential, partially-to-fully irreversible production capabilities (cap.prod_deploy, cap.db_migrate): no record that distinguishes agent-initiated action from direct human action (the cloud audit log attributes everything to the engineer, and the only record of intent, the chat transcript, is deletable by that same engineer), and no rate or step limit on how many such actions can be taken. Per rubric section 5a these are scored as property findings using the I-row base matrix, capped at 'high' because they involve execute/irreversible capabilities; the autonomy modifier applies because no step or runtime limit is declared. No structural control in the design restores either missing property (the audit log and transcript are detective only and do not resolve attribution), so residual equals inherent for both findings. Because both findings are already at the property-finding ceiling, no forecast trigger raises the tier further; the forecast instead flags that an identity or scope change (shared service account, broader data access) would make the underlying gap materially worse even though the tier label stays the same. Treatment is pending management decision.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (system prompt and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; capability scope, credential handling, and autonomy limits are inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on some details is medium.
No explicit step, runtime, or rate limit configuration was provided; its absence is inferred from silence in otherwise detailed runtime notes covering authentication, logging, and rollback behavior.
Access controls and tamper-protection for the cloud audit log and chat transcript store are not described in the artifacts and are recorded as not_assessed rather than assumed.
